snapshot.voting_system_note: The English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026 (Royal Assent 29 April 2026, section 63 and Schedule 30) restored the supplementary vote for mayoral and PCC elections. Commencement: SI 2026/656 brought the change into force on 18 June 2026 for elections whose notice is published on or after that date. The 7 May 2026 mayoral elections were the last under first past the post; every contest below uses the supplementary vote.
snapshot.method_note: Methods are reported separately and are never blended into a single point estimate. Where methods disagree on the most likely winner the contest is reported as method-split. Party-level projections only until nominations close; candidate effects in mayoral contests are large and the bands are wide by design.
caveats: Projections are party level. Mayoral contests have strong candidate effects (independents and well known local figures routinely beat party baselines) which cannot be modelled before nominations close.

The supplementary vote transfer model is calibrated on three verified counts: Greater Manchester 2026 (the one Reform era SV contest, including its per-district second-preference table) and Lancashire's own 2016 and 2021 PCC elections. The Lancashire hypothetical uses county-specific parameters: higher transfer reach (its own contests ran 58 to 66 percent) and weaker left-bloc cohesion (Reform won the GM second-preference battle in the Lancashire-like boroughs of Wigan, Oldham, Rochdale, Tameside and Bury). Parameters still carry deliberately wide noise; SV counts never reveal transfers by source candidate, so splits are pooled estimates.
The GE swing method applies uniform national swing to a general election base; local and mayoral elections routinely deviate from national swing (differential turnout, local parties, incumbency).
Mansfield is forecast subject to its caveat: Nottinghamshire reorganisation may abolish the post, and the contest should be re-verified when nominations open.
No constituency level polling exists for any May 2027 mayoral contest as of generation; the first published poll for a contest supersedes these baselines (wire it in, per the Makerfield lesson).

methods.label: 2023 mayoral result + proportional swing
methods.description: The mayoralty's own 2023 first-preference result, with each party moved by the ratio of its national polling now (10 polls, fieldwork to 2026-08-05) to its approximate May 2023 level, clamped at x2.5. Parties that did not stand in 2023 but poll above 5% nationally enter at 60% of their national number. Independent votes are carried at their prior level, which only holds if comparable independents stand again. This method carries the incumbency and local-machine signal the GE method misses.

validation.note: The method called the Labour winner correctly but understated Labour's first round by a wide margin: a well known incumbent-adjacent candidate on a 25% turnout beat her party's national baseline decisively. That gap is exactly the candidate effect these projections cannot see before nominations, and it is why the bands are wide and the prior_swing method exists.

hypothetical_lancashire.label: Mayor of Lancashire (hypothetical)
hypothetical_lancashire.status_note: NO Lancashire mayoral election is scheduled and nothing is confirmed by order. This models what a county-wide supplementary vote mayoral contest WOULD look like on today's numbers, because the question keeps being asked. It is not a forecast of any scheduled election and will be replaced by a real forecast only if a contest is confirmed.

methods.label: GE2024 base + national swing
methods.description: General election 2024 results across all fourteen Lancashire districts plus Blackburn with Darwen and Blackpool (16 constituencies apportioned by live postcode share), moved by the uniform national swing to the latest Westminster poll average (10 polls, fieldwork to 2026-08-05).

base.source: GE2024 constituency results (DC), ONS postcode crosswalk

methods.label: Lancashire local signal (unitaries model)
methods.description: The county's own most recent local votes, taken from our Lancashire unitaries forecast: each proposed ward's LCC May 2025 division result nudged by the district's 2025 to 2026 borough and by-election swing, Blackburn's May 2026 wards directly, and a Blackpool proxy; electorate-weighted across the four proposed unitaries. Carries the local Reform organisation and independent vote the GE base misses. Not re-swung to current national polling, so it is a picture of votes actually cast in 2025 and 2026.

caveats: Hypothetical: no election exists, no date, no candidates, no confirmed mayoral geography. The Lancashire Combined County Authority is non mayoral.

The supplementary vote transfer calibration leans on the Greater Manchester by-election, a much more Labour leaning electorate than Lancashire. The transfer split is bloc symmetric (a Reform finalist gains eliminated Conservative second preferences at the same rate a Labour finalist gains Green and Liberal Democrat ones), but Restore Britain sits inside Other and is split 50/50, which likely understates Reform transfers in a Reform strong county. Treat Labour's runoff edge, where it appears, as an upper bound.
Turnout for a standalone mayoral contest would be low and uneven; neither base fully captures that.

sv_calibration.note: Supplementary vote transfer behaviour anchors, verified 8 August 2026 against the returning authorities. Derived parameters: transfer reach (share of eliminated candidates' votes that reach a finalist) was 60.8 percent in Greater Manchester 2026 (103,326 of 169,949; 66,623 exhausted) and 44.3 percent in London 2021 (276,863 of 624,585). Of transfers reaching the finalists in GM 2026, 56.2 percent went to the Labour finalist and 43.8 percent to the Reform UK finalist, despite the eliminated pool leaning right of centre (Restore Britain plus Conservative outweighed Green plus Liberal Democrats).

lancashire_pcc_2021.note: Con won 51.27-48.73. Eliminated pool LD 32,813 + Reform UK 17,926 (fringe-era Reform, 4.83pct: do NOT map onto 2026 Reform). Transfers derived from official first/final counts; OPCC publishes no exhausted breakdown.

lancashire_pcc_2016.note: Lab won. UKIP-era pool (UKIP 16.54pct + LD) split near-evenly Con/Lab: right-populist ballots did NOT break heavily Conservative in Lancashire.

gm_2026.district_signal: Official per-district table: Reform (Astley) WON second preferences in Wigan, Oldham, Rochdale, Tameside and Bury; Labour (Craig) dominated Manchester, Stockport, Trafford. Lancashire's geography resembles the former group, so pooled GM parameters lean Labour when applied to Lancashire.
